newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seven French hurt in Bangui blast-French radio.
newsitem.headline: Seven French hurt in Bangui blast-French radio.

text.p: Seven French citizens working for the French embassy in the capital of the Central African Republic were injured by a mortar shell on Saturday, France Info public radio said.
It said the mortar apparently came from a camp held by former army mutineers. It gave no more details and French Foreign Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
Skirmishes between African peacekeepers and disaffected soldiers broke out on Friday.

A spokesman for the African force, deployed to help restore peace after three army mutinies in under a year, said a second Senegalese soldier had died as a result of the clashes, taking the death toll to three.

French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order after the most recent mutiny and handed over to the peacekeepers. The African force includes soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo.
